description:
Could You Stop an Asteroid From Hitting Earth?

Episode 111 of a daily journey through the universe. 🚀
We relive NASA's DART mission: on September 26, 2022 a spacecraft hit the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos at about 22,000 km/h and shortened its orbit by about 33 minutes; a 2026 study found it even nudged Didymos's path around the Sun, and ESA's Hera arrived in November 2026 to inspect the crash site.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 112: Next stop, asteroid samples. Bringing a piece of the sky home.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

Images: NASA (public domain)
Narration: AI voice

#space #dart #astronomy #shorts #science #nasa

segments.text: If an asteroid was coming for Earth, could we stop it? We already tried.
Could we stop an asteroid from hitting Earth? In twenty twenty-two, NASA tested it for real.
segments.headline: A real test

segments.text: The target: Dimorphos, a small asteroid moon about one hundred and sixty meters wide, orbiting a bigger asteroid, Didymos.
segments.headline: The target: Dimorphos

segments.text: On September twenty-sixth, the DART spacecraft slammed into it at about twenty-two thousand kilometers per hour.
It worked. Dimorphos's orbit got about thirty-three minutes shorter.
The crash blasted out a tail of debris thousands of kilometers long.
segments.headline: A huge debris tail

segments.text: In twenty twenty-six, scientists found DART even nudged the pair's path around the Sun. By a fraction of a second, but measurable.
segments.headline: Even the Sun orbit changed

segments.text: And in November twenty twenty-six, Europe's Hera spacecraft arrived to inspect the crash site up close.
segments.headline: Hera arrives

segments.text: The lesson: with enough warning, a small push can save a planet.
segments.headline: Early warning is key

segments.text: Tomorrow, two spacecraft that touched asteroids and brought pieces home. What they found inside surprised everyone. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
